extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of literary criticism; poets, critics, and scholars interested in Renaissance poetry and art criticism
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts aesthetic and critical criteria for judging Renaissance (Pleiad-era) poetry and related art criticism, and for assessing the qualities of a critic (Winckelmann). Emphasises style, music, historicity, individuality, and the critic's integrity and devotion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetry a la mode / historical interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Much of Du Bellay's poetry illustrates rather the age and school to which he belonged than his own temper and genius. Its interest depends not so much on the impress of individual genius upon it, as on the circumstance that it was once poetry a la mode, that it is part of the manner of a time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate work for its value as a representation or decoration of its historical moment: consider how successfully it embodies the 'manner of a time'. Such poetry may be important as cultural/historical evidence even if lacking strong individual originality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presence of style / unity of temper
rubrics_metrics.description: There is style there; one temper has shaped the whole; everything that has style, that has been done as no other man or age could have done it... has its true value and interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether a consistent temper or manner pervades the work. A distinctive, inimitable style confers true value even when subject matter is slight. Look for coherence of voice, recurring motifs, and an identifiable collective temper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intended audience / exclusivity
rubrics_metrics.description: It is poetry not for the people, but for a confined circle, for courtiers, great lords and erudite persons, people who desire to be humoured, to gratify a certain refined voluptuousness they have in them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whom the poetry is aimed at: elite/courtly audiences vs popular ones. Judge suitability of tone, references, and refinement to that intended circle; exclusivity can be a deliberate aesthetic choice rather than a flaw.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scholarship and pedantry (erudition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ronsard ... is anxious about orthography, about the letter e Grecque, the true spelling of Latin names in French writing ... His poetry is full of quaint, remote learning. He is just a little pedantic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note the presence of classical learning and pedantic detail (orthography, classical references). This may charm a learned audience but can date or alienate broader readers; weigh erudition against accessibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of foreign/coinéd words and ephemeral coinages
rubrics_metrics.description: A certain number of Greek words... and there were other strange words which the poets of the Pleiad forged for themselves, and which had only an ephemeral existence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate neologisms and foreign borrowings for their effectiveness and longevity. Are they playful and lively, or merely ephemeral affectations that do not integrate well into the language?

rubrics_metrics.name: Musicality / double music (meter + rhyme)
rubrics_metrics.description: To unite together these two kinds of music ... to make verse which should scan and rhyme as well ... to penetrate their poetry with a double music -- this was the ambition of the Pleiad. They are insatiable of music, they cannot have enough of it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge the poem's sonic qualities: meter, cadence, rhyme, and how they combine. Assess whether the verse attains a 'double music' (the strengths of both classical scanned verse and native rhymed song) and whether musicality enhances meaning rather than being mere ornament.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seriousness / weight of myth and subject-matter
rubrics_metrics.description: The old Greek and Roman mythology ... becomes with them a mere toy. That 'Lord of terrible aspect,' Amor, has become Love, the boy or the babe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine whether mythological or classical material is treated with depth and gravitas or merely as decorative play. Treating great themes frivolously may be an anti-pattern unless intentional irony or pastiche is evident.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone: raillery, diminutives, lightness
rubrics_metrics.description: They are full of fine railleries; they delight in diminutives, ondelette, fontelette, doucelette, Cassandrette.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess tonal register: playful raillery and diminutives signal a cultivated lightness. Determine whether that tone suits the poem's aims or undermines seriousness where seriousness is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authenticity of emotion / 'half-real' loves
rubrics_metrics.description: Their loves are only half real, a vain effort to prolong the imaginative loves of the middle age beyond their natural lifetime. They write love-poems for hire.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge emotional sincerity: are feelings vivid and genuine, or conventional/performative? Beware of formulaic amorous sentiment that reads as professionalized or commercialized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of death and vanity as ornament
rubrics_metrics.description: Their trite reflexions on the vanity of life ... the imagery of death serves for delicate ornament, and they weave ... trite reflexions on the vanity of life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether meditations on mortality serve genuine philosophical or emotional ends or are merely decorative motifs. Overuse as ornament can render such themes tired and insincere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grace and finish / perfection in minute detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Its merits are those of the old,--grace and finish, perfect in minute detail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appraise craftsmanship: polish, refinement, and careful finish in language and form. High finish can be a chief merit even when originality is not prominent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temper: subdued, delicate excitement versus vehemence
rubrics_metrics.description: A certain tenuity and caducity, as for those who can bear nothing vehement or strong ... a constant desire for a subdued and delicate excitement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine whether the poem's restrained, delicate temper is appropriate. Restraint can be an aesthetic choice; judge whether it produces desirable subtlety or flaccidity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Locality and landscape verisimilitude
rubrics_metrics.description: The poetry of the Pleiad is true not only to the physiognomy of its age, but also to its country ... the great Loire, with its long spaces of white sand ... It is full of the traits of that country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess how convincingly the poem evokes setting and local character. Authentic place-feel and recurring landscape traits enhance texture and cultural specificity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domesticity and homely goodness
rubrics_metrics.description: With this is connected a domesticity, a homeliness and simple goodness, by which this Northern country gains upon the South.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the presence of domestic, homely elements (fireside, winter pleasures). Such detail can root high culture in quotidian life and provide warmth and accessibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poesie intime / personal intimacy and individuality
rubrics_metrics.description: He ranks the Antiquites de Rome, and the Regrets ... as poesie intime, that intensely modern sort of poetry in which the writer has for his aim the portraiture of his own most intimate moods, and to take the reader into his confidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the degree to which the work presents intimate, personal mood and individual temperament. Intimacy can yield modern psychological resonance; weigh it against generic mannerism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sentiment for antiquity / ruins and transience
rubrics_metrics.description: He has this sentiment. The duration of the hard, sharp outlines of things is a grief to him ... the sentiment of the grandeur of nothingness -- la grandeur du rien.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the poet's treatment of antiquity, ruins, and transience: is it profoundly reflective or merely elegiac ornament? Authentic engagement with ruins can produce modern poignancy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form over matter / formal virtuosity
rubrics_metrics.description: It is a thing in which the matter is almost nothing, and the form almost everything; and the form of the poem as it stands, written in old French, is all Du Bellay's own.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge how much the poem depends on formal skill. Formal virtuosity can justify otherwise slight subject-matter when it creates a distinctive aesthetic effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capacity to transfigure the trivial (effects subtle and fleeting)
rubrics_metrics.description: A sudden light transfigures a trivial thing ... A moment -- and the thing has vanished, because it was pure effect; but it leaves a relish behind it, a longing that the accident may happen again.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the poet's ability to illuminate small incidents with sudden intensity. Such effects are often ephemeral; measure their frequency and whether they cumulatively produce durable meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critical originality: opening a new organ for the spirit
rubrics_metrics.description: Winckelmann ... by contemplation of the ideal works of the ancients, received a sort of inspiration, through which he opened a new sense for the study of art. He is to be regarded as one of those who ... have known how to initiate a new organ for the human spirit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For criticism, assess whether the writer proposes genuinely new sensibilities or frameworks that allow repeated return with renewed freshness. Original critical insight that reshapes perception is of highest value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Escape from abstract theory to sensory intuition
rubrics_metrics.description: Winckelmann ... escapes from abstract theory to intuition, to the exercise of sight and touch. He FIND[s] Greek art by direct handling and perception.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate criticism and scholarship by its grounding in direct, sensory engagement with works (sight/tactile description) rather than abstract theorising alone. Concrete handling often yields clearer insights for art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-minded devotion / selection of motive
rubrics_metrics.description: He renounced mathematics and law ... Nothing was to enter into his life unpenetrated by its central enthusiasm ... the development of his force was the single interest of Winckelmann, unembarrassed by anything else in him.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the value of focused, sustained devotion to a central aesthetic interest. Single-mindedness may produce deep mastery, though at the cost of other kinds of attainments; judge according to the critic/artist's aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrity / truth to type
rubrics_metrics.description: What affected Goethe ... was the integrity, the truth to its type, of the given force. Winckelmann's perfection is a narrow perfection: his feverish nursing of the one motive of his life ... The integrity, the truth to its type, of the given force.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether a work (or critic) remains true to its chosen aesthetic type or ideal. Integrity and fidelity to a coherent aesthetic principle are marks of excellence even if the scope is limited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enthusiasm as divinatory power
rubrics_metrics.description: Enthusiasm ... was the secret of his divinatory power over the Hellenic world. This enthusiasm ... has a power of re-enforcing the purer emotions of the intellect with an almost physical excitement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the role of passionate engagement in producing critical or artistic insight. Enthusiasm can be a legitimate epistemic force if accompanied by disciplined perception; mere fervour without discrimination is weaker.

rubrics_metrics.name: Higher cultured sensibility required for art
rubrics_metrics.description: The beauty of art demands a higher sensibility than the beauty of nature, because the beauty of art ... must be awakened and repaired by culture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When judging art, account for the need of cultivated sensibility: some works require informed cultural or formal sensitivity to be fully appreciated. Assess audience competence and whether the work rewards cultured attention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impartiality in aesthetic perception (male/female beauty)
rubrics_metrics.description: Those who are observant of beauty only in women, and are moved little or not at all by the beauty of men, seldom have an impartial, vital, inborn instinct for beauty in art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether the critic/reader possesses the requisite breadth of aesthetic sympathy. Narrow or gendered perceptual habits may limit one's capacity to grasp certain traditions (e.g., Greek male-figure emphasis).
